messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 03:12 UTC — node gpu-eu-07 in eu-west-1 reported CUDA_OOM events across multiple containers. Headroom reporting: 2.1GB available per allocator but kernels are failing. Auto-escalation to #incidents triggered. :rotating_light:

oncall-ryan: seeing this, pulling logs now. can someone confirm customer impact? pinging @cust-success-james

engineer-mei: attaching quick dumps — nv driver errors + allocator trace. Short summary: containers crashed with cudaErrorMemoryAllocation even though headroom metric showed ~2GB. Suspect fragmentation + reserved-block interaction with KV cache prefetch.

engineer-mei: ```
[2026-03-15T03:11:25Z] cuda malloc failed: cuMemAlloc 0x7f8a... size=256MB, error=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
nv-smi: GPU0  78% util  Memory-Used: 11.8GiB / 24GiB
allocator: headroom_reported=2147483648
allocator: reserved_blocks=3 sizes=[1.5G,512M,256M]
kv_cache: active_prefixes=4, prefetch_in_flight=2
fragmentation_score=0.67
```

oncall-ryan: meh. fragmentation_score 0.67 is high. Is this the same node that had recent prefetch changes? @engineer-mei any recent deploys?

engineer-mei: yes we rolled prefetch multiplier tweak last night to reduce cold latency. It increases background KV prefetch reservation. Might be holding a few large reserved blocks that look free but are unusable due to fragmentation.

sre-ana: immediate mitigations — 1) remove node from LB (drain) 2) stop KV prefetch on that node 3) restart inference runtime (graceful) 4) fallback affected requests to smaller-quantized model variant. Do steps 1-3 now? :thumbsup:

infra-bot: running: `kubectl cordon gpu-eu-07 && kubectl drain gpu-eu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

infra-bot: cordon ok, drain in progress — waiting for pods to terminate (eviction timeout 5m).

cust-success-james: customer acme-ml reported 503s from eu-west-1 starting ~03:10 UTC. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate model: gpt-large-infer. They've opened a support ticket #INC-1429. Please include expected ETA for rollback.

oncall-ryan: noted customer impact. posting a short update to ticket: "We detected CUDA allocation failures on a GPU node; mitigation in progress (draining node + restart). No data exfiltration. We will follow up with root cause and ETA."

engineer-mei: while drain is executing I pulled deeper allocator counters: `free_segments=12, largest_free=64MB, total_free=6.2GB but scattered; alloc_request_256MB_fails=7`. That matches OOM for medium allocations despite total free.

sre-ana: yes classic fragmentation: aggregate free > request but no contiguous chunk. Reserved_block metadata shows 3 large reservations that are partially pinned by KV cache and by in-progress allocations -> reduces usable contiguous. Recommend reducing reserved block sizes on next rollout and add a policy to compact small frees when fragmentation_score>0.5.

engineer-mei: for immediate hotfix I propose: i) disable prefetch on that node (already ordered) ii) trigger allocator compaction: `rtdbctl allocator compact --node gpu-eu-07 --target-contiguous=512MB` iii) restart runtime. Compaction may take ~30s and can increase latency for in-flight requests. Anyone object?

oncall-ryan: go for it. prioritize customer impact first.

infra-bot: exec: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/kv/disable_prefetch?node=gpu-eu-07` -> 200 OK

infra-bot: exec: `rtdbctl allocator compact --node gpu-eu-07 --target-contiguous=512MB` -> started, progress: 10%

engineer-mei: compaction progress: 50% now. observed largest_free increased to 512MB. retrying failing allocs in logs via synthetic test — synthetic 256MB alloc now succeeds.

sre-ana: once compaction done, restart runtime with graceful drain of connections: `systemctl restart redwood-runtime` on that node. Continue to monitor error rate and model fallback counts.

infra-bot: runtime restart scheduled. pods restarting...

engineer-mei: runtime reports healthy, no further CUDA_OOM in 90s window. nv-smi shows memory distribution improved: Memory-Used 8.2GiB / 24GiB across active containers. fragmentation_score down to 0.23.

cust-success-james: updated ACME ticket: "We applied a mitigation (node drain + allocator compaction + restart). Services restored for most traffic; we will monitor and follow up with root cause in a detailed postmortem." Customer accepted temporary workaround.

oncall-ryan: handing off to night oncall @oncall-simone for follow-up and postmortem. Key action items for follow-up: - add auto-detection for fragmentation_score>0.5 to trigger compaction fallback - reduce prefetch reservation default - add alert when largest_free < 256MB while total_free > 1.5GB - include fragmentation metrics in per-node dashboards

oncall-simone: acknowledged handoff. I'll take ownership for postmortem and coordinate with eng-ml on reservation defaults. ETA for full writeup: EOD today PST.

sre-ana: tagging runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-oom-fragmentation — will update with compaction step and KV prefetch checklist.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 03:24 UTC — node stabilized after compaction and restart. Final notes: impacted customer: acme-ml (partial), duration ~14m, mitigation path: drain -> disable prefetch -> allocator compaction -> restart -> service restore.

oncall-ryan: nice work team. follow-up owners: eng-ml (prefetch defaults) eng-runtime (compaction automation) perf (dashboarding). closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
